# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 77 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 49 | Coptic

---

## Saying 77

Jesus said: "I am the light that is over all things. I am the All. From me the All came forth, and to me the All attained. Split a piece of wood; I am there. Lift up the stone, and you will find me there."

---

**Council Notes:**

- This is arguably the most theologically rich saying in Thomas and one of the most discussed texts in early Christian studies.
- The "I am" structure echoes John's Gospel but with a distinctly cosmic, panentheistic character: Jesus is not just identified with light but with the totality (*ptērf*).
- "The All" (*ptērf*): capitalized in SOPHIA to mark it as a cosmic term. The All comes from Jesus and returns to Jesus — a circular cosmological statement.
- "Split a piece of wood / Lift up the stone": These lines assert divine immanence in the material world — the sacred hidden in the ordinary. They appear in a different location in POxy 1 (Greek fragment), confirming their early circulation.
- "To me the All attained" (*attain*/*aphikneomai*): the All "attaining" or "arriving at" its source — the eschatological return. LOGOS's "have returned" is interpretively richer but goes slightly beyond the Coptic.
- This saying has no Synoptic parallel. It is the definitive Thomas self-revelation of Jesus.
